audit_items.proof_trace: The only SELECT RLS policy for authenticated users on `member.members` uses `USING (true)`, granting every authenticated user unrestricted read access to all rows. No subsequent migration narrows this — `20260317000001_fix_security_permissions.sql` only revokes `anon` access, leaving the authenticated policy unchanged. The proof that non-admin users are restricted to their own row fails immediately: the USING clause imposes no row filter.
audit_items.attack_scenario: An authenticated user calls the Supabase PostgREST endpoint (`GET /rest/v1/members?select=*`) with their JWT; the `USING (true)` policy returns all member records, exposing every member's `student_number`, `discord_id`, `is_admin` flag, and other PII fields.
